pairs.locus: Boethius de Dacia, De mundi aeternitate 8
pairs.question: Dato enim hoc falso quod motus primus et mundus sit aeternus, numquid propter hoc erunt principia geometriae falsa, ut "a puncto ad punctum rectam lineam ducere", vel etiam "punctus est, cuius pars non est", et caetera talia, vel etiam suae conclusiones?
pairs.derivation: Author poses a numquid-interrogative and answers it himself. Question kept whole including the 'Dato... aeternum' supposition that fixes the referent of 'propter hoc'. Answer is the author's own self-reply 'Constat quod non.' immediately following the question. Editorial brackets: none in this span.

pairs.locus: Boethius de Dacia, De mundi aeternitate 8
pairs.question: Numquid omnes passiones possibiles in magnitudine eodem modo essent demonstrabiles de suis substantiis et per easdem causas, etiam si mundus esset aeternus, sicut et si mundus esset novus?
pairs.derivation: Second numquid-interrogative posed and answered by the author. The conditional 'etiam si mundus esset aeternus' is internal to the question, so it is self-contained. Answer 'Constat quod sic.' directly follows. Stripped editorial brackets around 'possibiles' (kept the word).
